newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end shade higher, seen listless.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end shade higher, seen listless.

text.p: Oblivious to the bulls on Wall Street, Argentine stocks closed modestly higher Friday as early gains melted away on profit-taking, dealers said.

"The market managed to soak up selling but it's been weakened," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers. "It wasn't inspired by the fact the Dow was surging into record territory, and the tone will probably remain hesitant early next week."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV added 0.6 percent to 540.59, slipping off a session high of 546.51, and showed a 1.6 percent gain for the week.

Traders shrugged off a surge in volume to 21.5 million pesos from 15.5 million Thursday, saying it reflected a combination of short-covering and profit-taking. "Buyers and sellers pretty much cancelled each other out," said Bonanno.
Over-the-counter deals picked up slightly to 120 million pesos from 117 million Thursday.

"Stocks are lagging bonds, which are drawing strength from Brazil's debt buyback scheme," said Adolfo Adorno of traders Agra. "The bolsa is waiting for quicker economic recovery and political cues, because Congress is not hurting the economy but it's undermining (President Carlos) Menem's position."
The ruling Peronist bloc in the lower house of Congress, which has an absolute majority, failed Wednesday night to garner quorum to pass a package of tax reforms.

Analysts noted the U.S. economic outlook was highly positive -- they said weak inflation data announced early Friday, unleashing Wall Street's buying frenzy, could persuade the Federal Reserve not to touch interest rates when it meets September 24.
"It seems to be the best-case scenario for the U.S. economy: growth financed by greater productivity, which keeps inflation at bay," said Adorno.
The prospect of stable interest rates coupled with Friday's drop in U.S. long bond yields below 7.0 percent could prompt many investors to seek higher returns in the emerging markets, dealers said.
In the session the broad market edged up 0.2 percent, with winners beating losers 36 to 10 and 13 stocks ending flat.

Top main-tier performers were oil company Sol Petroleo, carmaker Sevel and petrochemical concern Indupa, which jumped 3.8 percent, 2.9 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively. The heaviest loser was petrochemical firm Ipako, off 1.9 percent.
